instruction: In every month column from January to June, identify and visually mark the cell with the greatest sales value.

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting the maximum sales value in each month. Verified with Python: Jan max at (6,2)=767, Feb max at (10,3)=773, Mar max at (2,4)=722, Apr max at (7,5)=714, May max at (3,6)=730, Jun max at (7,7)=783. Evaluator checks if all 6 max cells are highlighted.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: checks if max value cells in all 6 month columns (Jan-Jun) are highlighted
Getter logic is correct: extracts highlighted cells from columns B-G (Jan-Jun), rows 2-11, and properly detects fill colors excluding default white
Metric logic is correct: compares highlighted cells against expected max cells and provides appropriate partial credit scoring
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' pattern: directly accesses expected.get('max_cells') since expected IS the rules dictionary returned by get_rule
Expected values appear correct: metadata shows Python-verified max values for each month with actual cell positions
Postconfig is appropriate: includes Ctrl+S to save Excel file before reading, ensuring highlighting changes are persisted
Data flow is sound: getter extracts state → metric compares → returns score based on correct highlights
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider penalizing extra unwanted highlights. Current metric only checks if expected max cells are highlighted but doesn't penalize if other non-max cells are also highlighted (e.g., solution where all cells are highlighted would pass). Could add: incorrect_highlights = len([c for c in highlighted_cells if c not in expected_max_cells]); penalty = incorrect_highlights / (len(expected_max_cells) * 2); score = max(0, correct_score - penalty)
